data.title: FPS Survival Forest Outpost
data.summary: Free 3D game assets for a first person survival shooter: a modular forest station kit, crafting and power, a palisade perimeter with traps, five invented weapons on a rarity ladder, vehicles and twelve rigged characters.
data.description: A complete set for a survival extraction shooter set in dense conifer forest, where a scavenger crew has fortified a half derelict logging and research station. The station kit is seventeen modules on a 4 m bay grid at a 3.5 m storey: corrugated and concrete wall bays, a window bay glazed and boarded, a hinged steel door bay, a tilting roller shutter bay, corner columns, floor slabs plain and with a stairwell, a stair flight, flat and pitched roof bays, a timber lookout tower with a ladder and a lit roof, a shipping container closed and standing open, a lean-to and a fuel shed. Sixteen pieces cover base building and crafting: a workbench with drawers and a lit lamp, a gunsmith bench, a scrap forge with a glowing firebox and worked bellows, a generator with a spinning flywheel, a fuel drum rack, a water purifier, a wind turbine, a solar array, a lattice radio mast with a swaying aerial and a red beacon, a tracking antenna dish, a two door steel locker, a shelving rack with crates that slide out, a hand ammunition press, a cooking fire with a pot, a drying rack and a tool wall. Thirteen pieces close and defend the perimeter: palisade bays and a two leaf gate, a sandbag wall, razor wire, chain link bays and a gate, a watch platform, a covered spike pit, a sprung bear trap, a tripwire flare, a punji line, a boarded barricade and a wrecked truck barricade. Twenty nine loot and gear pieces cover the five step rarity ladder on emissive rings, five original weapon archetypes with detachable magazines and moving bolts, slides or a break action, a recurve bow, a machete, backpacks, a plate carrier, a medical kit, bandages, a canteen, ration tins, an ammunition box, scrap and ore nodes, a fuel can, a lockbox, a supply crate, a landed supply drop, a field radio, a wind up torch and signal flares. Nineteen more give the world its vehicles and dressing: a quad, a battered pickup and a loaded logging truck with rolling wheels and opening cab doors, conifers in three sizes, stumps, a fallen log, boulders, undergrowth, ferns, a fuel bowser, oil drums plain and burning, pallet and tyre stacks, a floodlight mast, a hanging road sign and a campfire. Twelve figures finish it: a survivor scavenger, a masked raider, an armoured heavy, a scout with a bow, a field medic, a trader, a hazmat researcher, two infected variants, a stalker, a wolf and a boar. Every figure is a rigid jointed puppet of parented nodes on real joint pivots, with idle, head-turn, arm-swing and weapon-raise clips. Each is built to the tier: a shaped skull with a brow, a nose, cheekbones, a jaw and ears, eyes and a mouth in geometry rather than a texture, mitted hands with a separated thumb, layered clothing with a collar, a belt, straps, pockets and a hem with thickness, and boots with soles, toe caps and laces. There is no skeleton and no skin weighting anywhere in this pipeline, the fingers inside the mitt, the faces and the cloth are solid, and the legs are static so the feet stay planted. The pack is night capable by design: with no punctual lights in the pipeline, five emissive materials carry the light, on the fires, the furnace mouth, the floodlights, the screens, the warning lamps, the flares and the loot rings. The design is original throughout: no game names, logos, map layouts, callouts, operator or weapon names, no calibre designations, and no badges, insignia or lettering. Metre units, +Y up, +Z front, ground contact at y = 0.

starterScene.summary: A free survival game scene: a fortified scavenger outpost in dense conifer forest around a half derelict research station. A ring of timber palisade and chain link closes a 28 by 20 metre compound, with a two leaf palisade gate on the south track under a lit red lamp and...
starterScene.description: A free survival game scene: a fortified scavenger outpost in dense conifer forest around a half derelict research station. A ring of timber palisade and chain link closes a 28 by 20 metre compound, with a two leaf palisade gate on the south track under a lit red lamp and razor wire, punji stakes, a covered spike pit, a bear trap and a tripwire flare on the approach outside it. The station in the middle is built from the modular kit: two bays by two on the 4 m grid, two storeys of corrugated, concrete, window, boarded, door and roller shutter bays with a column in every corner, a deck and a stair flight between the storeys, and a flat roof carrying a solar array, a tracking dish and a legendary loot cache. In front of it the crafting yard is in use: the workbench with a carbine on it, the forge with its glowing firebox, the generator, the water purifier, the fuel drum rack, the drying rack and a steel locker, with the cooking fire and a campfire burning and a brazier going in a cut down drum. The lookout tower, the radio mast and the wind turbine give height at the back and a floodlight mast lights the yard. A pickup and a quad are parked inside. Loot is where a player would find it: four rarity caches, crates, an ammunition box, a lockbox, a medical kit, a pack, a plate carrier, a fuel can, scrap and ore. Eight figures are in play: the scavenger at the bench, the heavy on the gate, the scout on the tower with a marksman rifle beside her, the medic at the campfire, the trader by the container, a raider walking up the track, an infected in the trees and a wolf out in the forest. Static layout: the models keep their own clips, the scene adds none.

# Blender 4.x: File > Import > glTF 2.0, or from the Python console after downloading the file.
import bpy
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath='model.glb')  # from https://cdn.3dassets.dev/assets/32713/v1/model.glb

# Godot 4: copy model.glb into res://models/ and the editor imports it as a scene.
var packed := load("res://models/model.glb") as PackedScene
var model := packed.instantiate()
add_child(model)
